header.name: New Venture Planning
offered_to: B.Tech. post 4 semesters (students from 3rd year), M.Tech., and Ph.D.
header.description:
What tools do entrepreneurs need to successfully launch new ventures? What legal entity should a start-up adopt? How do entrepreneurs raise funds, establish a team and get their venture off the ground? What are the key ingredients of a successful start-up?
The curriculum is divided into 3 broad modules : Explore, Identify and Execute.
Module 1 - Explore : The first phase of Explore will engage with the personal dilemmas that entrepreneurs confront in the initial phases of their start up. It will further explore scanning for business opportunities with an entrepreneurial mindset. Examining new business models and some challenges involved in converting an idea into a business opportunity. Students will also understand how new markets can be created through entrepreneurial efforts.
Module 2 – Identify : The module uses the business model canvas (BMC) and the lean start up methodology to understand the importance of rapid prototyping and the need of a minimally viable product (MVP). A key lesson is the ability to rapidly prototype and move towards an MVP at the lowest possible cost and in the shortest time so that entrepreneurs can pivot on their initial ideas. This Module has lessons on bootstrapping and business model innovation.
Module 3 – Execute : Students also explore some issues on growth and profitability and the range of strategies that entrepreneurs have to choose from like market penetration, market development and related diversification. The class will discuss the process of how entrepreneurs form a venture (its legal identity) and the range of financing options available including bank loans, social media campaigns, venture funding (etc).
